Thought: The molecular formula C7H7Br matches perfectly with our mass spec data! The molecular mass of C7H7Br is 171 + 28 = 199, which matches the observed m/z of 199. The characteristic bromine isotope pattern in the mass spectrum (100:97.6 ratio for peaks at m/z 199 and 201) confirms the presence of one bromine atom. The fragments observed also support this structure, showing benzene ring fragments and CH2Br-related fragments. This is definitely benzyl bromide.
